    *   **Technology & Features?** (User-friendly app, budgeting tools, instant transfers)

    *   **Pros:** Extensive branch/ATM networks, wide range of products (loans, investments, credit cards), in-person service.

*   **Online Banks (e.g., Ally, Discover, Chime, Marcus):**
    *   **Pros:** Typically offer much higher interest rates on savings/checking, fewer fees, and innovative digital tools. Lower overhead costs mean better rates for you.
    *   **Cons:** No physical branches for in-person service. Cash deposits can be difficult or impossible. Reliant on customer service via phone/chat.

*   **Credit Unions:**
    *   **Pros:** Not-for-profit, member-owned. Often have lower fees, better rates on loans and savings, and more personalized customer service. Community-focused.
    *   **Cons:** May have fewer branches/ATMs (though many participate in shared networks). You must meet membership criteria (based on location, employer, or association).

*   **Local/Regional Banks & Community Banks:**
    *   **Pros:** Personalized service, local decision-making, deep community ties. Can be great for small business banking and building relationships.
